cards.name: Extrude1
cards.summary: Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows a pale-blue square with a box of depth behind it that recedes up and to the left: a bright cyan top face, a black left side, thin dark outlines, like a cube seen from the upper left. Applied to your own object it carries the extrusion direction, depth and shading settings, not the pale-blue square.
use_for: logos and headline blocks turned into 3D boxes
button and tile depth in infographics
avoid: Light from the right: use Extrude3, whose depth goes up-right and whose sides are dark navy.
Flat, print-simple artwork: the extrusion adds many faces; Object > Convert to Curves or Break Apart if the file is going to a cutter.
Thin text: the depth faces overlap and become hard to read; use a bold face and a shallower depth.
cards.applies_to: one vector object (closed shape, curve or text) selected with the Extrude tool: it adds depth faces as a live extrusion that keeps the source object editable
cards.how_to_apply: Toolbox > Effect Tools > Extrude (Automation.InvokeItem("c5555cfc-1c54-4c5b-ad28-60a4ec569798")): select the object, then pick 'Extrude1' in the Preset list on the property bar. Script: the harvest records no call that applies a .pst preset (the parameter block is undocumented); the file is Draw/Presets/VectorExtrude/Extrude1.pst in the CorelDRAW install folder. Scripted substitute: Shape.CreateExtrude(Type, VPType, VPX, VPY, Depth, Shading, BaseColor, ShadingColor, BevelDepth, BevelAngle, BevelColor, BevelOnly) set to match the preview (approximate; not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: Shipped preview: pale-blue square at lower right with depth receding up-left, cyan top face and black left side, as described.

cards.name: Blue Horizon
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Starter pack fill: a linear fountain (gradient) fill. Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows a vertical gradient, white at the top easing through light steel blue, then an abrupt step to a near-black navy band about half way down, which lightens through deep blue back to pale blue-white at the bottom: a sea or sky horizon with a sharp line.
use_for: dramatic dark-centre banner behind white type
avoid: A smooth, even gradient: it has a hard step in the middle; use Light Blue Sky for a smooth blue-to-white fade.
Text across the dark band: the contrast flips at the horizon line, so check legibility.
cards.applies_to: one vector object with a fill area (closed shape, text or a rectangle); the fill replaces the object's current fill and the object stays editable
cards.how_to_apply: Select the object, then in the Object Properties docker (Fill tab) open the fill picker and choose 'Blue Horizon' from the Starter pack content (the fill library in Corel Content > Fills); the harvest did not walk this route, so it is the usual one, not confirmed. Script: no call that applies a .fill file by name was found; rebuild it with Fill.ApplyFountainFill(StartColor, EndColor, Type = linear, Angle, Steps, EdgePad, MidPoint, BlendType, CenterOffsetX, CenterOffsetY) and add the intermediate stops with Fill.Fountain.Colors.Add. Harvested linear colour stops: 0% rgb(251,251,251), 48% rgb(97,154,180), 49% rgb(3,25,38), 65% rgb(10,76,107), 88% rgb(216,231,236), 96% rgb(252,253,253), 100% rgb(228,240,246).

cards.summary: CorelDRAW Starter pack fill: a repeating bitmap-tile fill. Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows a silver-grey diamond-plate (tread-plate) steel surface with raised diagonal lugs and a few rivets, tinted slightly pink and blue, as a repeating bitmap tile.
avoid: Very large objects: a bitmap tile repeats and softens when scaled up, so the repeat and blur show; raise the tile size only after checking at 100%.
Spot-colour or CMYK-critical print: the tile is a photographic bitmap, so its colours are RGB-derived and can shift.
Clean, minimal looks: the texture is busy; use Brushed Steel.
cards.applies_to: one vector object with a fill area (closed shape, text or a rectangle); the fill replaces the object's current fill and the object stays editable
cards.how_to_apply: Select the object, then in the Object Properties docker (Fill tab) open the fill picker and choose 'Textured Sheet Metal' from the Starter pack content (the fill library in Corel Content > Fills); the harvest did not walk this route, so it is the usual one, not confirmed. Script: no call that applies a .fill file by name was found; Fill.ApplyPatternFill(Type = cdrBitmapPattern, FileName, ...) and Fill.Pattern.TileWidth / TileHeight are the nearest calls (untested with this fill). Harvested tile size 1016000 x 1016000 tmicrons.

verified.note: Shipped preview: silver diamond tread-plate with raised diagonal lugs, a few rivets and faint pink / blue tints, as described.

cards.name: Yellow and Green Circles
cards.id: Content/Fills/Starter pack/Fountain Fill 069.fill#Yellow and Green Circles
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Starter pack fill: an elliptical fountain (gradient) fill. Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows soft concentric rings in alternating pale yellow, lime green and teal-green, centred near the upper left and repeating outward, like a ripple or target.
avoid: Text on top: the rings compete with letters; use a solid panel.
Calm, formal layouts: the pattern is lively.
cards.applies_to: one vector object with a fill area (closed shape, text or a rectangle); the fill replaces the object's current fill and the object stays editable
cards.how_to_apply: Select the object, then in the Object Properties docker (Fill tab) open the fill picker and choose 'Yellow and Green Circles' from the Starter pack content (the fill library in Corel Content > Fills); the harvest did not walk this route, so it is the usual one, not confirmed. Script: no call that applies a .fill file by name was found; rebuild it with Fill.ApplyFountainFill(StartColor, EndColor, Type = elliptical, Angle, Steps, EdgePad, MidPoint, BlendType, CenterOffsetX, CenterOffsetY) and add the intermediate stops with Fill.Fountain.Colors.Add. Harvested elliptical colour stops: 0% rgb(92,191,143), 31% rgb(226,217,123), 63% rgb(151,202,87), 100% rgb(224,216,123).
